Report_ID: Participants with any adverse event at 90 days (ITT)
Title: Thromboprophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin versus standard of care in unvaccinated, at-risk outpatients with COVID-19 (ETHIC): an open-label, multicentre, randomised, controlled, phase 3b trial
Author: Cools et al.
Comment: Descriptive only — no statistical test or effect estimate reported. Definition: 'any adverse event' at 90 days. Same construct as the 21-day adverse-event row; use only one per trial when pooling (90 days covers the full follow-up period).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneous for 21 days') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Country: Belgium, Brazil, India, South Africa, Spain, UK
Participant type: Unvaccinated outpatients aged ≥30 years with symptomatic, PCR-confirmed COVID-19 and ≥1 risk factor for severe disease
Outcome measurement: Number of participants with at least one adverse event of any type out of the number randomised in each arm, at 90 days
Outcome variable: Participants with any adverse event at 90 days (ITT)
effect_direction: More adverse events with enoxaparin (24/105, 23%) than standard of care (19/114, 17%) — RR >1, favouring control

Report_ID: Any adverse events (participants with at least one AE through day 35)
Title: Randomized Study of Rivaroxaban vs Placebo on Disease Progression and Symptoms Resolution in High-Risk Adults With Mild Coronavirus Disease 2019
Author: Ananworanich et al.
Comment: Denominators are the safety population (219 rivaroxaban / 230 placebo), not the number randomised (246 / 251); AE counts are only reported for the safety population, so the ITT denominator cannot be used. No RR/OR or P value reported for this row.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for 21 days') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Non-hospitalised adults (>=18 y) with mild COVID-19 at high risk for progression
Recruitment source: 13 US outpatient clinics in 7 states plus 1 virtual/decentralized site recruiting via social media (40 states)
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of participants in the safety population with any AE, Table 3
Outcome variable: Any adverse events (participants with at least one AE through day 35)
effect_direction: Essentially no difference; marginally more AEs with rivaroxaban (35/219, 16.0%) vs placebo (36/230, 15.7%) — RR ~1.02

Report_ID: Any bleeding event (participants with >=1 suspected bleeding event of any severity) within 45 days — adverse-event definition used: ANY BLEEDING EVENT
Title: Effect of Antithrombotic Therapy on Clinical Outcomes in Outpatients With Clinically Stable Symptomatic COVID-19: The ACTIV-4B Randomized Clinical Trial
Author: Connors JM
Comment: Denominators are the safety/efficacy analysis population (participants who initiated >=1 dose of trial medication: 144/135/143/136), not the numbers randomized (164/165/164/164). The paper states the primary analyses for efficacy and bleeding were limited to treatment initiators and that bleeding counts among all randomized participants are reported only in eTable 2 of Supplement 3, which is not included in the provided text; therefore the initiator (safety population) denominators are used, as flagged. Pooled treatment events/totals obtained by summing the three antithrombotic arms exactly as reported, per the plan's multi-arm rule; no risk ratio was reported by the paper (only risk differences).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Antithrombotic therapy pooled (aspirin 81 mg once daily + apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily + apixaban 5 mg twice daily)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Symptomatic but clinically stable outpatients aged 40-80 years with newly diagnosed SARS-CoV-2 infection
Recruitment source: 52 US clinical sites, institutional/regional COVID-19 test reports and commercial outpatient testing centers
Outcome measurement: Count (%) of participants with any bleeding event per assigned treatment group among those who initiated trial therapy (Table 2)
Outcome variable: Any bleeding event (participants with >=1 suspected bleeding event of any severity) within 45 days — adverse-event definition used: ANY BLEEDING EVENT
additional_group_ns: Arm-level counts among treatment initiators (Table 2): aspirin 6/144 (4.2%); apixaban 2.5 mg 9/135 (6.7%); apixaban 5 mg 13/143 (9.1%); placebo 3/136 (2.2%). Pooled antithrombotic group = 6+9+13 = 28 of 144+135+143 = 422. Numbers randomized were 164 (aspirin), 165 (apixaban 2.5 mg), 164 (apixaban 5 mg), 164 (placebo) = 657.
effect_direction: More bleeding events with pooled antithrombotic therapy (28/422, 6.6%) than placebo (3/136, 2.2%) — RR >1, favouring control

Report_ID: Adverse events (serious adverse events) within 30 days
Title: Enoxaparin for primary thromboprophylaxis in symptomatic outpatients with COVID-19 (OVID): a randomised, open-label, parallel-group, multicentre, phase 3 trial
Author: Barco et al.
Comment: The paper reports serious adverse EVENTS (8 vs 9), not explicitly the number of participants with at least one SAE; however 16 of the 17 events corresponded one-to-one to the 16 primary-outcome events (8 patients per arm) and the 17th occurred in a separate standard-of-care patient, so event counts here equal participant counts. Denominators are the ITT randomised numbers (234/238). No RR, CI or p value is reported by the paper for this outcome.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Enoxaparin 40 mg (4000 IU anti-Xa) subcutaneous once daily for 14 days') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomised controlled trial (open-label, parallel-group, multicentre, phase 3)
Participant type: Outpatients aged 50 years or older with acute symptomatic COVID-19, clinically stable, eligible for ambulatory treatment
Recruitment source: Eight hospital study centres in Switzerland and Germany (test centres, general practitioners, study hotline)
Outcome measurement: Count of serious adverse events in each arm, denominator = number randomised (ITT)
Outcome variable: Adverse events (serious adverse events) within 30 days
effect_direction: Slightly fewer serious adverse events with enoxaparin (8/234, 3.4%) than standard of care (9/238, 3.8%) — RR slightly <1

Report_ID: Adverse events defined as any bleeding (combination of major, clinically relevant non-major, and other bleeding)
Title: Rivaroxaban versus no anticoagulation for post-discharge thromboprophylaxis after hospitalisation for COVID-19 (MICHELLE): an open-label, multicentre, randomised, controlled trial
Author: Ramacciotti et al.
Comment: Denominator is the ITT population (159 per arm) rather than the number randomised (160 per arm); two patients (one per group) withdrew consent and were excluded from the ITT analyses, and the paper reports safety analyses only on the ITT population. Adverse-event definition used = any bleeding (major + CRNM + other), as no overall adverse-event total was reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rivaroxaban 10 mg/day for 35 days after discharge') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adults discharged after hospitalisation for COVID-19 at increased VTE risk (IMPROVE VTE score >=4, or 2-3 with D-dimer >500 ng/mL)
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with at least one bleeding event (major, CRNM, or other) out of patients in the ITT population per arm
Outcome variable: Adverse events defined as any bleeding (combination of major, clinically relevant non-major, and other bleeding)
effect_direction: More bleeding with rivaroxaban (4/159, 2.5%) than no anticoagulation (3/159, 1.9%) — RR 1.33 (0.30–5.86), favouring control, not significant
